Gamma-integral representation of $1/n^{s+1}$ and summation to the Bose-type integral giving $\Pi(5)\zeta(6)$
Substitution $x=e^{-y}$ giving cot integral over $(0,\infty)$, then $y=\pi t$

Relation between the $y^5/(e^y-1)$ integral and an integral over $1/(e^{2\pi t}-1)$
Partial-fraction decomposition over roots of unity
